To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a minimal basis for the hamiltonian of the pairing force is given by composite bosons of zero angular momentum and two, and that the eigenvectors of given energy, angular momentum and seniority are expanded in the composite bosons minimal (irredundant) basis with coefficients expressed in terms of generalized hypergeometric functions.
a minimal basis of composite bosons, having the remarkable symmetry property that the number of bosons is the same in every state of a given seniority, is set up for the pairing hamiltonians.

1) the eigenfunctions of the pairing hamptonian can be expressed in terms of the minimal basis, 2) the minimal basis can be expressed in term of composite boson states with angular momentum zero, two, and four, 3) the coefficients of the minimal basis expansion are given by a generalized hypergeometrc function of the energy, seniority, angular momentum and the pairing interaction.

the construction of a minimal basis in the space of the Grassmann algebra, which allows to solve the pairing hamiltonians with the lowest angular momentum and seniority.
the construction of a minimal basis of the pairing Hamiltonian in the space of even Grassmann variables using composite bosons.
a generalization of the Balian-Salomon model of pairing.

the pairing hamiltonians eigenvalues and eigenvectors are obtained in a simple and straightforward manner using a minimal basis of composite bosons.
the composite bosons formalism, in spite of its limitations, is still a useful tool for a qualitative description of pairing correlations in nuclei.
the minimal basis is a powerful tool in the study of the pairing hamiltionian.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a minimal basis is set up and a method for the exact diagonalization of the pairing hamitonian is developed.
a minimal basis for the Hamiltonian is constructed, and the eigenvalues and eigenfunctions are found for given energy, seniorities and third component of the total angular momentum.
the pairing hamiltonians are exactly solvable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the pairing problem is a special one and the use of composite boson techniques is not justified.
the minimal basis for the seniority-zero eigenfunctions of the pairing hamiltomian is the same for any value of the angular momentum.
the pairing problem is a problem of composite bosons, and the minimal basis we found is the natural basis for this problem.
